_comment: Phase 4 (F-04) single source of truth for network egress. Consumed by src/core/egress-policy.ts (runtime enforcement) AND scripts/check-bundle-hosts.mjs (post-build tripwire). Keep both readers in sync by editing ONLY this file.
_allowlist: Hosts the shipped code actually FETCHES. Exact, lowercase, no scheme, no port.
_hostPatterns: Regional hosts whose middle label is concatenated at runtime. A hostname matches when it starts with `prefix`, ends with `suffix`, and the single label in between matches [a-z0-9-]+ (so `oidc.evil.example.amazonaws.com` does NOT match). Every suffix here must be a namespace AWS itself controls: a suffix under which anyone can self-register a subdomain (`.awsapps.com`) would hand a hostile build a ready-made allowlisted destination.
_loopbackHosts: http: is permitted only for these (Ollama / LM Studio / OAuth loopback listener).
_knownDocHosts: Hosts that appear as literals in the bundle but are NEVER fetched: documentation links, links opened in the user's browser, and placeholder examples. `ai-gateway.vercel.sh` is the `ai` SDK's built-in default gateway — it is deliberately listed HERE and NOT in `allowlist`, so the tripwire passes while the policy blocks any request to it. `d-xxxxxxxxx.awsapps.com` is the SSO-start-URL placeholder shown in the settings description; the SSO start URL is only ever sent as a field in the body of a request to oidc.<region>.amazonaws.com, never fetched.
_knownRuntimePrefixes: Truncated literals the bundle contains because the region is concatenated at runtime (`https://oidc.` + region + `.amazonaws.com`). The bundle scanner sees the prefix only, so it is accepted verbatim.
